title: Direct Identification through PII Collection
description: Registration collects personally identifiable information (name, email, government ID) that directly identifies the parent user, creating inherent identifiability risk.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Government ID
description: Government ID is highly sensitive personal data that, if disclosed to unauthorized parties, could lead to identity theft, fraud, or other privacy violations.

title: Excessive Data Collection for Authentication
description: Collecting government ID and six-digit code may exceed data minimization principles for authentication purposes, potentially collecting more data than necessary.

title: Linkability of Registration Data to External Sources
description: Email and government ID could be linked to other databases or services, potentially enabling correlation attacks across multiple data sources.

title: Identifiability of Parent Account Data
description: The MongoDB users collection stores parent account information that can be used to identify individuals. If accessed by unauthorized parties, this data could reveal personal identities and account relationships.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Parent Account Data
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, insufficient encryption, or security vulnerabilities in the database system.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Parent Account
description: Parent account data in MongoDB could be tampered with or modified by unauthorized actors, leading to authentication failures, account hijacking, or incorrect parent-child relationship mappings.

title: Linkability of Parent Account Data
description: Parent account data processed by the Authentication Service could be linked to other data flows or systems, potentially enabling correlation attacks that reveal additional information about users.

title: Usurpation of Parent Account Identity
description: The Authentication Service could be vulnerable to identity usurpation attacks where unauthorized actors attempt to impersonate parent accounts, potentially through credential theft or session hijacking.

title: User Identifiability via JWT Token
description: The JWT token sent to the parent user contains user identity information that could be used to identify the individual, potentially exposing personal data to unauthorized parties if the token is intercepted or mishandled.
assumptions: JWT contains identifiable user information; transmission may not be fully encrypted

title: User Data Disclosure During Transmission
description: User data transmitted alongside the JWT could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties if the communication channel is compromised or if the data is logged/stored insecurely at the parent user endpoint.
assumptions: Transmission channel may not be fully secure; parent user endpoint may have inadequate data protection

title: JWT Token Usurpation and Impersonation
description: An attacker who obtains the JWT token could potentially impersonate the authenticated user, gaining unauthorized access to services or data associated with that user's identity.
assumptions: JWT tokens may be stolen or intercepted; insufficient token validation at receiving endpoint

title: Excessive User Data in JWT Payload
description: The JWT token may contain more user data than necessary for the authentication service's purpose, violating data minimization principles and increasing the privacy risk if the token is compromised.
assumptions: JWT payload may include unnecessary user attributes; data minimization not fully considered

title: Linkability of Child Login to Parent Identity
description: Child's login activity using parent credentials can be linked to parent's identity through the parent email, creating a persistent association between child activities and parent identity.
assumptions: Parent email is used as identifier in authentication logs

title: Direct Identification of Child Through Parent Credentials
description: Child's identity is directly identifiable through the authentication process using parent email and password, potentially revealing parent-child relationship.
assumptions: Parent email is unique identifier

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Parent Credentials
description: Parent email and password transmitted during child login could be intercepted or logged by the authentication service, leading to unauthorized access to parent account.
assumptions: Credentials transmitted over network

title: Excessive Data Collection for Child Authentication
description: Collecting parent email and password for child login may exceed data minimization principles, as child could authenticate with child-specific credentials.
assumptions: Parent credentials are not strictly necessary for child authentication

title: Credential Usurpation by Third Parties
description: Child's parent credentials could be stolen or compromised, allowing unauthorized third parties to impersonate child or parent during authentication.
assumptions: Credentials stored or transmitted insecurely

title: Potential Violation of Child Privacy Regulations
description: Using parent credentials for child login may violate child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA) requiring separate consent and authentication mechanisms for minors.
assumptions: Applicable jurisdiction has child privacy laws

title: Child User Identifiability via JWT and Profiles
description: The JWT token and child profiles transmitted from the Authentication Service contain personally identifiable information that can be used to identify the child user across systems and contexts.
assumptions: JWT tokens and child profiles contain unique identifiers or quasi-identifiers that can be linked to the child user.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: Child profiles may contain sensitive personal information (e.g., health data, location, family information) that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the JWT is compromised or intercepted during transmission.
assumptions: Child profiles contain sensitive PII; JWT tokens can be intercepted or stolen.

title: JWT Token Theft and User Impersonation
description: JWT tokens transmitted from the Authentication Service could be stolen or intercepted, allowing an attacker to impersonate the child user and access their profile data or perform actions on their behalf.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted over networks where interception is possible; tokens may not have adequate expiration or revocation mechanisms.

title: Excessive Data Collection in Child Profiles
description: Child profiles may contain more personal data than necessary for the authentication service's legitimate purpose, violating data minimization principles and increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: Child profiles include fields not strictly required for authentication or service delivery.

title: Non-compliance with Child Data Protection Regulations
description: Transmission of child profiles and JWT tokens may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy laws requiring special protections for minors' data.
assumptions: The system handles data of children under 13/16 depending on jurisdiction; regulations require explicit consent and enhanced protections.

title: Linkability of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) could be linked with other data sources to create a comprehensive profile of the child, potentially enabling tracking across systems or services.
assumptions: Data is stored in multiple systems or shared with third parties

title: Direct Identification of Child
description: The combination of government ID, name, DOB, and gender in the child profile enables direct identification of the child, creating privacy risks if accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Government ID is a unique identifier

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Data
description: Sensitive child profile information including government ID could be disclosed to unauthorized individuals or systems through security vulnerabilities or improper access controls.
assumptions: Data is transmitted or stored without adequate encryption

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: Child profile data could be tampered with during creation or storage, leading to incorrect or fraudulent information being recorded in the system.
assumptions: Insufficient input validation or access controls

title: Identity Usurpation
description: An attacker could usurp the child's identity by creating a false profile using stolen or fabricated information, potentially leading to identity fraud.
assumptions: Government ID verification is not robust

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation
description: Without proper audit trails or digital signatures, it may be impossible to prove who created or modified the child profile, leading to accountability issues.
assumptions: No cryptographic proof of origin is implemented

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB collection could be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient, exposing sensitive personal information about children.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data could be altered by unauthorized actors, potentially leading to identity fraud, false information, or manipulation of child records.

title: Direct Identification of Children
description: Child profile data contains personally identifiable information that could directly identify children, creating privacy risks if exposed or mishandled.

title: Linkability of Child Data Across Systems
description: Child profile data could be linked with other datasets (e.g., school records, medical data) to create comprehensive profiles, increasing privacy risks.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violations
description: Storage and processing of child data may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other child privacy regulations if proper consent, age verification, and data minimization are not implemented.

title: Linkability of Video Search and Interaction History
description: Child user's video search queries, likes, and comments can be linked across sessions to build a comprehensive profile of viewing preferences and interests, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's activities and interests.
assumptions: System logs all interactions and maintains persistent user accounts

title: Identifiability Through Video Content and Comments
description: Video content uploaded or commented on by the child user may contain personally identifiable information (PII) such as names, locations, or other identifying details that could be extracted and used to identify the child.
assumptions: Child users may inadvertently include PII in video content or comments

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Content and User Data
description: Video content, search history, and interaction data could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, improper access controls, or sharing with external services without proper consent.
assumptions: System may have vulnerabilities or share data with third-party services

title: Excessive Data Collection for Video Management
description: The system may collect more video data and user interaction information than necessary for the stated purposes of video search, request, like, and comment functionality, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: System collects metadata, viewing history, and interaction logs beyond what's needed for core functionality

title: Account Usurpation and Impersonation
description: Child user accounts could be compromised or impersonated, allowing unauthorized individuals to access video content, post comments, or perform actions on behalf of the child user.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be weak or accounts may be shared among family members

title: Insecure Data Storage and Transmission
description: The Video Management Service may store or transmit video content and user data without adequate encryption or security controls, increasing risk of interception or unauthorized access.
assumptions: System may have insufficient security measures for data protection

title: Video metadata linkability to individuals
description: Video metadata (timestamps, locations, device IDs) could be linked to specific individuals, enabling tracking of movements and activities across time and space.
assumptions: Metadata contains or can be correlated with identifying information

title: Video content reveals identifiable individuals
description: Video files may contain visual or audio content that identifies individuals (faces, voices, activities), potentially exposing private information without consent.
assumptions: Videos capture identifiable people in private or semi-private settings

title: Unauthorized access to video files and metadata
description: MongoDB data store could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to exposure of video content and associated metadata to individuals without proper authorization.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities in MongoDB

title: Unauthorized video upload or retrieval
description: Malicious or compromised users could upload videos containing private content or retrieve videos they should not have access to, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Authentication/authorization controls are insufficient or bypassed

title: GDPR compliance violations with video data
description: Storage and processing of video metadata and content may violate GDPR requirements for consent, data minimization, and right to erasure, especially for biometric data.
assumptions: Video data contains biometric information and is processed without adequate legal basis

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Search and Watch History
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection storing child search and watch history may be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient, exposing sensitive behavioral data about the child.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Child History Data
description: Child search and watch history stored in MongoDB could be tampered with or modified by unauthorized actors, potentially altering the child's behavioral profile or creating false records.

title: Identification of Child from Search and Watch Patterns
description: Analysis of search and watch history patterns could potentially identify the child or reveal sensitive information about their interests, location, or activities, leading to unwanted identification.

title: Linkability of Child History to Other Data Sources
description: Child search and watch history could be linked with other data sources (e.g., device IDs, timestamps, location data) to create a comprehensive profile of the child's behavior and activities.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data Storage
description: Storing child search and watch history may violate child privacy regulations such as COPPA or GDPR-K if appropriate consent mechanisms, data minimization, and retention policies are not implemented.

title: Video Content Identifies User
description: Video data inherently contains identifiable information about the user, including facial features, voice, and personal context that can be used to identify the individual.
assumptions: Video content is processed and stored without sufficient anonymization or masking techniques.

title: Unauthorized Video Disclosure
description: Video data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during storage, transmission, or processing phases of the video management service.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls, encryption, or audit logging mechanisms are in place.

title: Video Data Tampering
description: Video content could be altered, modified, or corrupted during upload, approval, or storage processes without detection.
assumptions: Lack of cryptographic integrity checks or digital signatures on video data.

title: Cross-Context Linkability
description: Video data could be linked to the user across different systems, time periods, or contexts, creating a comprehensive profile.
assumptions: Video metadata or content is shared or accessible across multiple platforms or services.

title: Privacy-Obfuscating Controls
description: The approval/rejection interface may lack adequate privacy controls or transparency, making it difficult for users to understand how their data is handled.
assumptions: User interface does not provide clear privacy settings or data usage information.

title: Child identification from video stream
description: The video stream may contain identifiable information about the child, including facial features, voice, or other biometric data that could be used to identify the child.

title: Unauthorized access to video stream
description: The video stream could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing the child's activities or location.

title: Linking video data to child identity
description: Video data from the stream could be linked to the child's identity through metadata, timestamps, or other identifiers, creating a comprehensive profile.

title: Child impersonation in video access
description: An unauthorized party could potentially impersonate the child to access or receive the video stream, compromising the intended recipient.

title: Child Identification from Browsing Data
description: Child browsing data in the MongoDB collection could be used to identify the child, especially if combined with other data sources or metadata. This poses significant privacy risks for minors.
assumptions: Data contains identifiable information or can be linked to identifiable records

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Browsing Data
description: Sensitive child browsing data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through the data flow to the AI engine, potentially leading to privacy violations and regulatory non-compliance.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or data transmission security

title: AI-Driven Data Manipulation of Child Profiles
description: The AI Recommendation Engine could manipulate or alter child browsing data, potentially creating misleading profiles or recommendations that affect the child's experience and privacy.
assumptions: AI system has write access or can modify stored data

title: Linkability of Child Data Points
description: Different data points about the same child could be linked together across the data flow, creating a comprehensive profile that reveals more than intended about the child's behavior and preferences.
assumptions: Multiple data attributes are collected and transmitted

title: Non-Compliance with Child Data Protection Regulations
description: The data flow may violate child-specific privacy regulations such as COPPA or GDPR-K, given the collection and transmission of child browsing data to an AI system.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements are not fully addressed in the data flow design

title: Linkability of Browsing Data Across Sessions
description: Browsing data sent to advertisers may be linked across different sessions or devices, enabling profiling of individual users over time.
assumptions: Advertisers maintain persistent identifiers or use device fingerprinting techniques.

title: Identification Through Browsing Behavior Analysis
description: Browsing data shared with advertisers could be analyzed to identify specific individuals, revealing personal interests, habits, or sensitive information.
assumptions: Advertisers have sufficient data volume and analytical capabilities to perform user identification.

title: Excessive Data Collection Beyond Necessity
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may share more browsing data than necessary for the advertising purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Data sharing agreements do not strictly limit the scope of browsing data transmitted.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure by Advertisers
description: Third-party advertisers may mishandle or leak the browsing data they receive, exposing it to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Advertisers have inadequate security controls or share data with their own partners without proper safeguards.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violations
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if proper consent and legal basis are not established.
assumptions: Data sharing occurs without explicit user consent or legal basis required by applicable privacy laws.

title: Direct Identification of Data Subjects
description: Government ID images contain personally identifiable information that directly identifies individuals, making them highly sensitive to privacy breaches.

title: Linkability of ID Images to Other Data Sources
description: Stored government ID images can be linked to other datasets (e.g., transaction records, biometric data) creating comprehensive profiles of individuals.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of ID Images
description: File system storing government ID images may be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities.

title: Data Manipulation of Stored ID Images
description: ID images in the file system could be altered, tampered with, or replaced by malicious actors compromising data integrity.

title: Identity Usurpation via Stolen ID Images
description: If ID images are compromised, attackers could use them to impersonate individuals for authentication or fraud purposes.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Storing government ID images may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations requiring strict handling of sensitive personal data.

title: JWT Token Disclosure via XSS Attack
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage are vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, allowing attackers to read and exfiltrate authentication tokens through malicious scripts.
assumptions: Attacker has access to the browser environment and can inject malicious scripts

title: User Identity Usurpation via Token Theft
description: Stolen JWT tokens can be used by attackers to impersonate legitimate users, gaining unauthorized access to protected resources and performing actions on behalf of the user.
assumptions: Attacker obtains valid JWT token and has network access to protected endpoints

title: JWT Token Modification via localStorage Manipulation
description: Attackers can modify JWT tokens stored in localStorage, potentially altering claims or creating forged tokens to bypass authentication checks.
assumptions: Attacker has browser access and can modify localStorage contents

title: User Data Linkability Through Token Claims
description: JWT tokens may contain user identifiers and claims that can be linked to other data sources, enabling profiling and correlation of user activities across systems.
assumptions: JWT contains identifiable user information and other data sources exist for correlation

title: User Identifiability Through Token Exposure
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage can expose user identity information to attackers, making users identifiable even without active authentication.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity claims and attacker can access localStorage

title: Non-Compliance with Security Best Practices
description: Storing JWT tokens in localStorage violates security best practices and may violate regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR, OWASP guidelines) regarding secure authentication token storage.
assumptions: Regulatory or organizational security policies require secure token storage mechanisms

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child history
description: Child's historical data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches, violating the child's privacy expectations.
assumptions: System has adequate access controls but may have vulnerabilities; parent has legitimate access rights.

title: Child identification through profile data
description: Child's profile history may contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify the child, even when intended for parent review only.
assumptions: Child's data includes identifiers or quasi-identifiers that could enable re-identification.

title: Excessive data display to parent
description: System may display more child history information than necessary for parent review, violating data minimization principles and exposing sensitive details.
assumptions: System displays comprehensive history rather than filtered/summarized data.

title: Linkability of child data across systems
description: Child's history data could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, medical data) creating a comprehensive profile beyond parent's intended review scope.
assumptions: Data may be shared or accessible across multiple systems; uncertainty about data integration practices.
